data.narrative:
Bravo Ordnance is a Seed-stage Defense & Security company that has raised $3.6M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic—spanning Seed through Series A stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method uses $4M (total raised as a proxy) and applies a typical Seed-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.5x, implying a $9M valuation. The Peer-Median method examines five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $125M (NODA AI) to $4.0B (Stark Defence), yielding a median of $1.0B. This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity within early-stage defense tech, where venture capital deployment varies significantly by technology differentiation and customer validation.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $8M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median cross-section of $504M. The wide range reflects material uncertainty typical of Seed-stage companies: stage-progression methodology anchors toward the lower bound given minimal operational data, while peer-median approaches pull toward venture-backed defense tech norms. Key uncertainties include customer traction, technical validation, and regulatory pathway clarity—factors that will substantively narrow this range at Series A.
